Right now at this state of the game I unfortunately have to give a negative review because of 2 reasons: Reason 1: I like the idea that you need to load your spells on your fingers, HOWEVER there is this extremely annoying curse mechanic where you basically lose fingers until you decide to unlock them again, but also get a penalty. Now that in itself would be bearable, if it wasn't 90% of enemies using this mechanic. So you're constantly having your fingers cursed, breaking them, having them cursed again, breaking them again, while the enemy get's stronger with every turn and you're not advancing and just die after a while. Reason 2: The game is way too hard. I did 4 runs and didn't even manage the first boss. Now there maybe are people who manage it, but I don't and I don't even know what I'm doing wrong. The game is from the beginning on way too hard, but you also don't even unlock any stuff between runs to make it easier or anything like in other roguelikes. Every run starts at the same frustrating difficulty and meets the same frustrating end. I'm not even motivated to try further because I know that I will just loose again and spent time for nothing. The game was promising but is in the end a huge disappointment.

玩法有创意，且把该特色变成一个体系的游戏。此游戏特色是手，其一切设计：卡牌、遗物、敌人意图均围绕此展开。但是并不好玩，成长曲线太不合理。具体见后边讨论缺点。 不同于常见的费用出牌机制，本游戏使用元素槽——玩家的手作为每回合回复的费用，使用各种元素作为卡牌的费用，玩家需要规划元素放置，尽可能以最佳顺序打出最好的牌。 本游戏的遗物以戒指的形式套在各个手指上，在该手指引导某种特定元素法术时，就会触发戒指效果。玩家需要规划戒指摆放顺序，让增益尽可能最大化。 敌人也会与玩家的手互动。敌人会给手指上诅咒。玩家下一次在被诅咒的手指上引导元素时，会激发诅咒。诅咒包括直接对玩家造成伤害、给予玩家减益、给予敌人增益等。玩家需要寻找低压回合，在合适的时间解除诅咒。 当然此游戏也有缺点。体量太小了。不过毕竟小作坊，可以理解。 第一局玩下来，感觉怪物没几种，戒指来来回回就那几个。卡牌倒是不算少，但没什么特别基米的卡牌，都挺朴实无华。只要抓住左脚踩右脚的配合就能通关。 第二局玩第2个角色，前期纯区，一直叠力量蠕动。第一个boss拿了Lethal会全部应用于一张攻击，结果发现Lethal不吃Power加成，惊天一条区......然后蠕动到第2个boss，拿到100伤aoe直接气笑，直接通关。 可见此游戏的成长曲线过于糟糕。普通卡和道中的戒指很难质变。我只能在boss获得强反馈。 此外，本游戏升级机制纯敷衍，所有升级均为+1，不管你是伤害还是nb的Buff（100伤攻击升级后变101我是真气笑了），如果卡牌会给自己上debuff，就还有-1层debuff的升级分支。

I tend to not write negative reviews since they aren't as fun to write but this is an exception. Pluto is a proof-of-concept, not a game ready for release, even given its generous price point. There are many flaws with the game, but it had serious potential that is unfortunate to see squandered. I was drawn in by its grunge and evocative artwork and the the alluringly intuitive and evocative concept of using fingers as a resource to cast spells that are cards, but it fails to deliver on its promises. The core mechanisms of the game (finger economy + sigils matter) is not meaningfully built upon by the game and by hour 3, there were vestigial gameplay loops that crowded out the cool finger spellcasting. Instead, as you progress, you will find the following gameplay loops: 1) shockingly uninspired resource management (heat), 2) underwhelming sigils management (rings), 3) shallow persistent resource management. There is a more pressing issue which I think need to be remedied: The lack of a traversable data set. A huge draw of rogue-lites is the ability to hone your intuitions and understandings of the data set(s) the game presents. This cannot be done when the elements you play with are too randomly generated or contradictory. In Pluto, cards will have the same name but different effects, costs, and uses. Some cards will cost an identical amount, be named the same, and then have wildly different gameplay ramifications. It's frustrating and signals to me that I shouldn't trust the game and that its data set isn't worth learning. Moreover, the exceptionally few types of encounters one can have in the game make for same-y playthroughs where the biggest decision you make is after the first boss. The relatively limited choice-tableau creates situations where there are very few questions you ask yourself when making decisions. While I do not claim to be an expert at the game (and I do not want to spend the time to do so), I found the sheer number of "strictly better" options across runs staggering. This is compounded by the same few challenges being present in every attempt. There is a shockingly low number of "questions" the game asks of your deck. This crowds out strategy and means that a huge portion of tools fail to have places in the game. I feel a twinge of guilt sharing my thoughts on this game because it is obviously made as a labor of love. Its art is gory and detailed, and there is a beautiful heart of a creative vision here. I just wish that heart had been polished and refined more before being made to power a clumsy homunculus forced to run a marathon. I wish I returned this game. EDIT: This game also would benefit from a more robust soundscape. Its dreary ambiance and purely atmospheric music fits but gets old quick and leaves much to be desired. Would really benefit from some tunes.

tldr: I both loved the game and hated many parts of it. If you like deckbuilding roguelikes and you like the art, its worth buying in a sale. If you don't like the art, the deckbuilding part is lacking in true variety but still bearable. After finally finishing a run for each character, I was both very impressed and unimpressed by the game. I love the artstyle, the music, even the idea that these ancient wizards are going to their niece's party amidst the most horrible looking world ever. I hated that although each wizard has different spells, passives, and even the order you had to place your spells in hand, all the wizards pretty much needed the same items (specifically badges that would give extra draw, armor, and damage rings). Aside from the paladin and the flame knight, I pretty much only used armor or damage rings. I really wished there was more boss variety too, especially after beating the game at least once.

really good. I am IN LOVE with the art style and sound design. Notably, however, games with this kind of artstyle often are lacking in the gameplay department (which is fine and makes sense, they are usually more-so artistic projects, and are still an enjoyable experience). Which is why I cannot recommend Pluto enough, because the gameplay is also amazing and addicting. Think slay the spire meets darkest dungeon 2, with a unique combat system I have never seen before. A combat system that fully succeeds in both being fun, being surprisingly deep, and most of all working with the overall atmosphere of the game. There are only 3 things I wish were different: 1. first and foremost, I REALLY wish there was a compendium similar to slay the spire. There is a knowitorium that shows a gallery of the gifts, but its lacking any real stats. I always enjoy looking at my winstreak, total wins, etc. In slay the spire on the compendium, and between that + the heart damage carrying between runs, it adds a surprising amount of replay value to me. I feel like this wouldn't be hard to implement, either. Just something to show the "work" ive put into, if I play the game for 100 hours and win abunch, for example. 2. Runs aren't long enough, in my opinion. IIRC there are 2 bosses per run, the mini-boss and the final boss (who is always the same by the way, but its a new game and the final boss is well-designed so I'll let it slide). But when I reach the final boss, progression-wise it feels like a pretty abrupt ending because I hadn't had a ton of time to have fun with my now designed build for that run. And it just feels kind of strange that you only get 1 gift per run, it heavily encourages you to slot into a single archetype. Making a run longer, thereby forcing a player to do a dual-archetype for any given character would make runs more varied, probably 3. there are some balancing-kinks, although its a new game so I'm not worried. But some things are just clearly overpowered, and some things are terrible (maybe a skill-issue, but for example on the apprentice, the spell that gives you feeble, or really any spell that gives you feeble is literally never worth playing, and it sticks out pretty badly because afaik there is no way to remove a spell from your deck, and hand size is a pretty important aspect of the game and that character). I think its moreso that there are a decent chunk of terrible spells rather than op spells, which can do a good job of building the atmosphere of a darkest-dungeon-esque (I am constantly in fear) thing, but when it goes too far (feeble spells on apprentice where I am playing them maybe once every 5 fights cos i have nothing better to do) it feels silly Overall amazing game, I'll continue to keep playing, really hope some cool mods come out and/or it keeps getting updated.

What is this game? A deckbuilding roguelike ( like slay the spire ? ) but with several interesting mechanical differences. Cards are comprised of effects and elements; If you play a card with a certain combination of elements, and it contains the element combination of another card in your hand; that other card is also played... And you assign the elements to your fingers... This sounds insane : ) There are several characters, I was afraid it would be repetetive to try other characters... It is markedly not, as the ones I've tried have markedly different mechanics each of them... So, go get your hands. ( thumbs not included )
